t:
(a) 
Public Law 90–408, as amended, is amended under the heading “Inside the United States”, in section 201 as follows:

        (1) 
With respect to Naval Submarine Base, New London, Connecticut, strike out “$1,225,000” and insert in place thereof “$1,825,000”.
  
    (b) 
Public Law 90–408, as amended, is amended by striking out in clause (2) of section 802, “$239,082,000” and “$245,947,000” and inserting in place thereof “$239,682,000” and “$246,547,000”, respectively.

fable.w: This section only amends dollar amounts in a prior military construction authorization act. There is no tempting reading here: it involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision.
fable.s: With respect to Naval Submarine Base, New London, Connecticut, strike out “$1,225,000” and insert in place thereof “$1,825,000”.

qwen_block.w: This section amends appropriation amounts for specific military bases. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process involving parties outside the federal government. The text is purely administrative and financial, adjusting funding levels without referencing public comment, advisory boards with non-federal members, or consultation with states or tribes.
qwen_block.s: With respect to Naval Submarine Base, New London, Connecticut, strike out “$1,225,000” and insert in place thereof “$1,825,000”.

opus.w: This section only changes dollar amounts in Public Law 90–408 for military construction at Naval Submarine Base New London and in the section 802 totals. No one outside the federal government is consulted, and the section creates no hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking authority, or right to sue. A reader might be tempted to call any amendment to a law procedural, but changing funding figures involves no outside participation in a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: The section solely amends specific dollar amounts in existing laws regarding appropriations for naval bases. It does not establish any advisory committees, public comment periods, consultations with non-federal entities, or rights to sue. The actors involved are implicitly Congress (amending the law) and the federal agencies receiving funds, all of which are inside the federal government.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing appropriation amounts implies a decision-making process involving stakeholders, but the text itself only lists numerical changes to statutory funding levels. It does not describe any process of consultation, hearing, or input from outside parties.
